result.summary: This PR adds a new -outboundbind=<addr> option that binds outgoing clearnet (IPv4/IPv6) connections to a specified local source address, one per address family, separate from the existing -bind option which only affects listening. It validates the address at startup via LookupHost and a trial bind() (mirroring how -bind validates via BindListenPort), rejects ports, the wildcard, and Tor/I2P/CJDNS values, warns when a proxy makes the option inert for a family, and aborts (without fallback) a connection whose source bind fails at connect time. It includes unit tests for per-family selection and the bind-before-connect path, and a functional test exercising both families end to end.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core has no way to control the local source address of outgoing connections; multi-homed hosts and hosts behind specific network interfaces are stuck with whatever the OS routing table picks, and issue #6476 (open since 2013) asks for this to be configurable.

resolved_concerns: luke-jr worried this could break load-balanced outbound setups; author argued outbound connection count is capped and small, and the concern did not recur.

gmaxwell objected that extending -bind semantics would surprise LAN/bridge users by breaking local connectivity; author redesigned the feature as a separate -outboundbind option rather than changing -bind, which vasild then concept-ACKed.

frankomosh and vasild raised numerous review comments (CNetAddr storage, LookupHost port rejection, trial-bind validation, wildcard handling, precedence, comment clarity, test coverage); author implemented fixes across several force-pushes through 2026-08-19 and vasild gave an approach ACK on the resulting commit.
winterrdog gave an approach ACK, only noting a personal naming preference (-exitbind) as a non-blocking aside.

result.card: This PR adds -outboundbind=<addr>, letting operators pin the local source address used for outgoing clearnet (IPv4/IPv6) connections, one address per family, without altering existing -bind listening semantics. It solves a real, long-requested problem for multi-homed and VPS hosts (issue #6476, open since 2013) where the OS routing table otherwise picks the outbound interface. The PR went through a substantive redesign after gmaxwell warned that extending -bind itself would break LAN/bridge connectivity, and now carries concept/approach ACKs from vasild, frankomosh, and winterrdog with no outstanding objections. It includes functional and unit test coverage for both families, startup validation via trial bind(), and fail-closed behavior on a failed source bind. Reviewability is Ready; no dependency blocks it and it directly closes #6476.
